L52: # Clinical Studies
L53: 
L54: A clinical study is a carefully designed investigation used to evaluate certain aspects of the diagnosis or treatment of a specific medical condition. The goal is to find new and better ways to prevent, diagnose or treat diseases of dogs and cats. MedVet’s Clinical Studies Center facilitates high-quality clinical studies to advance the veterinary profession in caring for our beloved pets.
L55: ## Current Clinical Studies
L56: 
L57: We have successfully completed single center and multi-center clinical studies evaluating diagnostic tests, pharmaceuticals, biologics, surgical procedures, and medical devices for acute and chronic pain, congestive heart failure and other cardiac diseases, osteoarthritis and other orthopedic diseases, cancer, seizure disorders, endocrine diseases, ophthalmologic conditions, and chronic skin diseases. You can explore our current clinical studies below.
L58: ### Experimental EGFR/HER2 Tumor Vaccine
L59: 
L60: This is a USDA regulated scientific study. Enrollment is limited to dogs with osteosarcoma, hemangiosarcoma and transitional cell carcinoma. The
L61: vaccine is currently provided at no charge to the pet owners. As this is not a fully funded study, all costs associated with hospital visits, diagnostics and vaccine administration are the responsibility of the pet owner. If the vaccine receives approval, it will no longer be provided at no cost.
L62: To ensure all patients meet the enrollment criteria of having an expected prognosis that is greater than three months, MedVet hospitals are currently limiting enrollment to patients who are receiving appropriate standard of care therapies which may include surgery, chemotherapy, and/or radiation therapy depending on the tumor type. Patients being screened for enrollment with the intent to use the vaccine as a single agent treatment will not be considered.
L63: #### Study Locations
L64: 
L65:   * MedVet Salt Lake City is currently enrolling patients.
L66:   * MedVet Cincinnati and MedVet Cleveland enrollment is limited to established patients with all treatment and follow-up visits being held at the same hospital.
L67:   * MedVet Pittsburgh enrollment is limited to dogs that live in Pennsylvania with all follow up visits being held at MedVet Pittsburgh.
L68:   * MedVet Chicago is currently pausing enrollment until further notice.
L69: #### Study Enrollment Criteria
L70:   * Histologically (biopsy) confirmed diagnosis of osteosarcoma, hemangiosarcoma, or transitional cell carcinoma. An exception may be made if the dog has a long bone (limb) lesion consistent with osteosarcoma and the owner has elected not to pursue amputation. If amputation is planned, the first dose of vaccine can be administered following the amputation.
L71:   * Anticipated survival of greater than 3 months as determined by the evaluating oncologist. While dogs with metastases may be enrolled in the study, this will be based on the extent/volume of disease and prognosis.
L72:   * Dogs cannot be enrolled if they are receiving other immunotherapies or alternative therapies or are enrolled in another clinical study. Traditional chemotherapy and radiation therapy are allowed.
L73: #### Required Testing
L74:   * All costs associated with evaluation and testing are the responsibility of the pet owner and are not covered by the study. You will be provided with a cost estimate for all required and any additional recommended testing.
L75:   * Chest X-rays, CBC, biochemical profile, and urinalysis at baseline prior to vaccine administration. Testing completed within seven days will likely be acceptable.
L76:   * Chest X-rays must be repeated at three, six, and nine months.
L77:   * A blood sample will be collected at each visit (baseline, day 21, day 40-50, three months, six months, nine months) for research purposes.
L78:   * Strict adherence to the vaccine administration guidelines is required. A booster vaccine must be given 21 days following the initial dose. It is allowable to administer the booster one day early or up to seven days late if necessary due to appointment availability or if the administration day falls on a weekend or holiday.
L79: #### Contacts
L80: 
L81: For questions, e-mail clinicalstudies@medvet.com.
L82: 
L83: ### Immune-mediated Keratoconjunctivitis Sicca ("Dry Eye")
L84: 
L85: 【71†MedVet Columbus】 is currently enrolling dogs diagnosed with immune-mediated Keratoconjunctivitis sicca (“dry eye”) in a clinical study evaluating the use of an investigational new drug in the treatment of KCS in dogs.
L86: #### Study Eligibility
L87:   * Dogs must be ≥ 6 months old
L88:   * Diagnosis of KCS based on history and/or ophthalmic examination
L89:   * Schirmer Tear Test (STT) of ≥ 2 mm/minute and ≤ 10 mm/minute in one or both eyes
L90:   * Dogs must have a score of 2 or above on at least 2 of the 3 conjunctival signs associated with KCS
L91:   * Pet owner must be willing to comply with the protocol restrictions and the visit schedule
L92:   * Dogs with chronic medical conditions (for example, endocrinopathies, cardiovascular conditions, atopy, etc.) are permitted, but such conditions must be stabilized prior to enrolling the dog in the study and these animals must not be receiving prohibited concomitant medications
L93: #### Exclusion Criteria
L94:   * Dogs with non-KCS ophthalmic conditions that require one or more ophthalmic medications (e.g., glaucoma)
L95:   * Dog diagnosed with KCS at < 6 months of age in order to exclude dogs that may have congenital alacrima
L96:   * Suspected neurogenic KCS
L97:   * History of removal of the third eyelid gland in the affected eye(s)
L98:   * KCS associated with a diagnosis of canine distemper
L99:   * History of parotid duct transposition in the affected eye(s)
L100:   * Punctal plugs in the affected eye(s)
L101:   * Non-healed corneal ulcers
L102:   * History of local radiation therapy in the ocular region
L103:   * Other exclusion criteria not listed above will be discussed with you, include certain prohibited concomitant medication
L104: #### Study Information
L105: Your dog will be screened to confirm that it fulfills the inclusion/exclusion criteria for this study. During screening, procedures include obtaining medical history, physical examination, blood and urine collection, obtaining a body weight, and an eye examination will be performed. This is a randomized, masked, negatively-controlled trial. Your dog will be randomly assigned to receive the investigational drug or a negative control product (sterile buffered saline).
L106: Neither you nor your veterinarian will be aware of whether your pet is assigned to receive the investigational drug or negative control product. Patients will be randomly assigned based on order of eligibility for enrollment to one of the two treatment groups in a 2:1 ratio of investigational drug to negative control product.
L107: If your dog is enrolled in the study, you, the owner/undersigned, will be asked to administer treatments to your dog pursuant to Sponsor’s instructions, which will be provided by your veterinarian.
L108: #### Pet Owner Savings
L109: Your dog will receive treatment under this study, including all tests, procedures, and medications, at no cost to you. If your dog has an allergic reaction or is injured as a result of participating in the study, the Sponsor will work with your veterinarian to cover reasonable expenses related to treatment of such reaction or injury. There are no additional expenses for participating in this study.
L110: If your pet is excluded or removed from the study, but requires continued care for eye disease, future examinations and procedures will NOT be covered by the research study. An estimate of costs for which you will be responsible will be prepared for you at the time of admission.
L111: #### Contact
L112: 
L113: If you are interested in the study and would like to learn more, please reach out to Dr. Terah Webb.­
L114: 
L115: ### Chronic Inflammatory Enteropathy
L116: 
L117: 【72†MedVet Dayton】, 【73†MedVet Mandeville】, and 【74†WestVet Boise】 are currently enrolling dogs with chronic inflammatory enteropathy (CIE) in a clinical study evaluating the effectiveness of an investigational monoclonal antibody.
L118: #### Study Information
L119: Dogs will be screened to confirm that they meet the inclusion/exclusion criteria. Screening diagnostics include upper and lower gastrointestinal endoscopy with biopsies, blood and fecal testing, and imaging. Patients that qualify will be randomly assigned to receive either the investigational product or a control product (placebo). Pet owners must be willing to commit to the study visit schedule over a 130-day period.
L120: Pet families will be required to assess and record clinical signs of CIE during the study.
L121: #### Study Eligibility
L122:   * Eligible dogs will have a history of chronic, intermittent vomiting, diarrhea, inappetence/anorexia, and/or weight loss for a minimum of three weeks prior to screening.
L123:   * Must not have any other serious concurrent illnesses such as hepatic or renal disease, cancer, diabetes, Addison’s disease, Cushing’s disease, or any other disease that could interfere with the study results.
L124:   * Must not be positive for gastrointestinal (GI) parasites, histoplasmosis, or schistosomiasis at the screening visit.
L125:   * May not have significant panhypoproteinemia and/or marked ascites at the screening visit.
L126:   * May not have evidence of GI obstruction or mass at the time of screening.
L127:   * May not have or suspected of having exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.
L128:   * May not have a history of any surgical procedure in the past 30 days or any GI surgery within the past six months prior to screening.May not be on any prohibited medications within the following time frame prior to screening.
L129:     * One week: Dewormers, anti-diarrheal
L130:     * Two weeks: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS)
L131:     * Four weeks: Short acting steroids, pancreatic enzyme supplements, vaccines, Apoquel
L132:     * 12 weeks: Long-acting steroids, immunosuppressive agents, alkylating agents, Cytopoint
L133:     * Not allowed: Mitotane, Trilostane
L134: #### Pet Owner Savings
L135: 
L136: This is a funded study that includes testing, procedures, medication, and food (all directly related to this study and its requirements) at no cost to pet owners. In the event of an adverse event, the study sponsor may cover reasonable expenses related to participation.
L137: 
L138: #### Referral Incentive
L139: 
L140: Referral partners are eligible for a $200 gift card from the study sponsor for each patient that is screened and enrolled in the study.
L141: #### Contact
L142: 
L143: To learn more about this study, please reach out to one of the following Internal Medicine departments:
L144: 
L145:   * MedVet Dayton: 937.496.5306; im.dayton@medvet.com
L146:   * MedVet Mandeville: 985.626.4826; im.mand@medvet.com
L147:   * WestVet Boise: 208.375.1600; internalmedicine@westvet.net
L148: # Contact Us
L149: 
L150: If you have a pet that you believe may qualify for a clinical study, please contact your family veterinarian. We will work with them to determine if your pet is eligible and could benefit from participation in the study. If you are a veterinarian with a patient that you believe could benefit from a clinical study, please contact us.

L160: ## Frequently Asked Questions
L161: ### What is a clinical study?
L162: The purpose of a clinical study can vary. For example, the goal may be to determine the effectiveness of a new medication or combinations of medications. Clinical studies can also be used to determine how new procedures can improve quality of life or shorten recovery time for surgical patients.
L163: The results from large, multi-center clinical studies are used by both the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) in the approval process for new drugs and biologicals (vaccines, therapeutic antibodies) for companion animals. Clinical studies used in the approval process are conducted according to the Good Clinical Practice (GCP) recommendations, a set of international guidelines that ensure the highest standards.
L164: Participation in a clinical study is strictly voluntary and requires the pet owner’s written permission. Not every pet qualifies for participation in a clinical study. Communication between our doctors and your family veterinarian is maintained to determine what is best for your pet.
L165: ### What is the benefit of a clinical study?
L166: 
L167: Participating in a clinical study can be rewarding for you and your pet, and you play an important part in helping your own pet as well as future pets. Many medical and surgical treatments are available today because of the participation of pets in clinical studies.
L168: MedVet’s Clinical Studies Center leads collaborative initiatives with our veterinary specialists and veterinarians worldwide. We complete clinical studies by working in partnership with a wide array of investigators, from university faculty members to biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors. The outcome of these important studies benefits our entire veterinary community by putting safer, more effective treatments into the hands of veterinarians here and around the world in support of better patient outcomes.
L169: ### What are the advantages of my pet participating in a clinical study?
L170: 
L171: Clinical studies are well designed to provide the best opportunity to play an active role in your pet’s health care and gain access to new treatments before they are widely available. Your pet will receive expert medical care and close monitoring. Patients enrolled into a clinical study may receive professional services, diagnostic testing, or medical treatments and medications at reduced or no cost, depending on the study.
L172: ### What are the drawbacks to my pet participating in a clinical study?
L173: As with any medical treatment or procedure, clinical studies are not completely risk-free and may require extra time on your part. There may be side effects of the treatment being studied, or the new treatment may not be as effective as hoped. However, treatments used in clinical studies have been rigorously evaluated before advancing to the point of clinical evaluation.
L174: Also, clinical study patients are monitored very closely to minimize the chance of any negative effects and e nsure participating in the study is the best option for your pet’s ongoing health care.
L175: ### How do I enroll my pet in a clinical study?
L176: If your pet has a condition or disease we are currently studying, ask your veterinarian to contact the primary study veterinarian. Working with your veterinarian, the study veterinarian can determine if your pet is a po tential candidate. Then, you would meet with the clinical investigative team at MedVet to discuss the study details.
L177: You will sign an “informed owner’s consent” document if you elect to have your pet participate. There may also be some screening diagnostics to complete before you r pet becomes enrolled. For example, a patient with kidney disease might not be eligible for study, so a blood test would be part of the screening process.
L178: ### Can I withdraw my pet from a clinical study after it has started?
L179: 
L180: Yes. You have the right to withdraw from a clinical study at any time for any reason.
L181: ### I’m sponsoring or collaborating on a clinical study; can I work with MedVet?
L182: MedVet’s Clinical Studies Center has worked with a variety of sponsors, from professional to private foundations, to facilitate completion of high-quality clinical studies in client-owned dogs and cats. We can assist you in your development efforts, from pilot investigations through multicenter GCP pivotal efficacy studies.
L183: We’re both flexible and creative and foster good working relationships with a goal of ensuring studies are completed in a timely fashion and in compliance with all standards of current Good Clinical Practice (GCP/VICH GL9) guidelines.
L184: Dr. Jon Fletcher, Director of Post-Graduate Medical Education & Clinical Studies, and Edna Moore, Clinical Studies Supervisor, have extensive experience managing and internally monitoring GCP studies. They work with the Clinical Investigative Teams located throughout our organization to ensure all aspects of a study run seamlessly from start-up, patient recruitment, data collection, site monitor and regulatory agency visits, to study close-out processes.
L185: Our strength lies in our ability to recruit many qualified patients in a short period. With an integrated system of more than 35 specialty and emergency hospitals, we have a large and varied caseload of more than 500,000 patients annually. We are also fortunate to have a referral network of more than 7,500 veterinarians who value the role clinical studies play in helping their current and future patients.

L7: ## What we do
L8: 
L9: CASTR Alliance aims to advance human and veterinary medicine by facilitating the discovery of innovative treatments through the management of high-quality veterinary clinical studies and collaboration with industry leaders and veterinary hospitals.
L10: 
L11: We provide turnkey management of sponsored veterinary clinical studies to pharmaceutical and medical device development teams worldwide.
L12: We partner with state-of-the-art veterinary specialty and referral hospitals throughout the Pacific Northwest and beyond to enroll patients on sponsored clinical studies.
L13: 
L14: We manage sponsored clinical trials that abide by Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards for veterinary studies and are designed to ensure the collection of high-quality data.
L15: We submit all CASTR-run studies for ethical review by an external Veterinary Clinical Studies Committee (VCSC) to prioritize the safety and well-being of all patients.
L16: 
L17: 【4†MORE DETAILS】
L18: ## What motivates us
L19: 
L20: The motivations behind CASTR Alliance’s efforts are to connect companion animals with cutting-edge treatments, address naturally occurring diseases in pets, and accelerate medical innovation for both animals and humans through clinical trials.
L21: 
L22: #### Linking Patients to Caregivers
L23: 
L24: Our sponsored studies link companion animals in need of innovative solutions to novel therapeutic or diagnostic options that may otherwise be unavailable to them.
L25: #### Studying Spontaneous Diseases
L26: 
L27: Our research focuses on spontaneous diseases – those that arise naturally in dogs and cats. By enrolling companion animals who are already afflicted or symptomatic, we aim to provide potential direct benefits to our pets while gathering data that could help human or animal patients in the future.
L28: 
L29: #### Accelerating Medical Innovation
L30: 
L31: When a pet is enrolled in a CASTR-managed clinical trial, they take part in helping advance medical discovery and innovation.
L32: ## 【5†Translational research:】 Caring for our pets while advancing human and animal healthcare
L33: 
L34: ## What to expect
L35: 
L36: #### Contracting companies
L37: 
L38: can expect all CASTR Alliance-run studies to be managed efficiently and ethically, adhere to GCP standards, and result in high quality data. We deliver progress updates upon request throughout the trial, conduct diligent site and safety monitoring, and provide data at interim analysis, and at the conclusion of the trial.
L39: #### Veterinary clinicians
L40: 
L41: and support staff participating in the study are trained from the onset on the trial protocol to ensure treatment is conducted according to our rigorous standards. We continue to provide guidance and support to our participating sites throughout the entire course of the study.
L42: #### Pet owners
L43: 
L44: who enroll their pets in these clinical studies engage directly with a participating veterinary center, where all study procedures are carried out in accordance with the established study protocol. Studies are typically supported such that treatment is partially or fully covered by the sponsor.
L45: ## WHO WE ARE
L46: CASTR Alliance was founded in 2019 by veterinary clinician-scientists Jessica Bertout and Jim Perry. As scientists, they bring extensive experience in designing, managing, and conducting clinical trials that meet the rigorous standards of the biotech industry. Moreover, as devoted pet owners and veterinarians, they are personally committed to delivering the highest quality care for our animal companions. Together, Drs.
L47: Bertout and Perry created CASTR Alliance to leverage their expertise and advance medicine for humans and animals alike.
